events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to St. Joseph by boat.** My expectation is a rating of about 1 (below average). Muskegon is close behind at about 1. South Haven looks slow (about 0), and Grand Haven has no recent boat report, so I'd rate it 0 until one comes in.
- Start in 30 to 60 feet of water, and cover the 10 to 60 foot range if the first pass is empty.
- Troll small crankbaits and spoons. Chartreuse and green spoons were the colors that worked at Muskegon.
- Expect a few fish, not a steady bite. Keep moving along the lines that produce.

## Why
- St. Joseph had the most active boat reports of the four ports: coho and Chinook both caught, with small crankbaits and spoons working best (St. Joseph, 2023-04-26).
- Muskegon's only salmon boat catch was Chinook trolling 30 to 60 feet of water on chartreuse and green spoons, rated below average (Muskegon, 2023-04-26).
- South Haven's boat fishing was rated slow for salmon (South Haven, 2023-04-26), so I'd expect it to be the weakest choice this week.
- I'd expect Grand Haven to stay slow for now. Its last reports described dirty Grand River water slowing the action (Grand Haven, 2023-04-20), and it has no boat salmon report in the last four weeks.

## Evidence
**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph (2023-04-26): "Boat anglers targeting coho were catching a few fish … spread out from 10 to 60 feet of water," with some anglers "well over 100 feet." Chinook were "an occasional" catch. Both were rated below average.
- Muskegon (2023-04-26): "Boats trolling in 30 to 60 feet of water caught a few Chinook salmon … Chartreuse and green spoons worked well." Rated below average.
- Muskegon (2023-04-20): boats trolling the shoreline found it "slow for brown trout and coho salmon" (rated slow).
- South Haven (2023-04-26): "Boat anglers targeting salmon also had slow fishing" (rated slow).
- Grand Haven (2023-04-20): "Dirty water from the Grand River has slowed the action" (rated slow). No boat report at Grand Haven in the last four weeks.
- Pier reports were slow to fair at all four ports. This matters only if you change plans.

**Past seasons (history, not current conditions)**
- Past seasons with similar surface temperatures (satellite near-pier water about 46 F) mostly gave boat ratings of 0 to 1 in late April and early May.
- The one strong boat week was St. Joseph on 2022-05-04: coho rated good (3) in 30 feet of water, with a few Chinook deeper near 60 feet. That week had heavy upwelling winds, and the surface was warmer than this year's (buoy 50 F).

**Conditions now**
- I couldn't get live conditions. The tool returned a backtest summary for the week before 2023-05-02, so I don't have a current buoy reading or a current 3-day trend.
- That summary showed buoy water at about 45 to 46 F across the ports, and the satellite near-pier water at about 45 to 47 F. Wind gusts reached 44 to 47 mph, and north-to-east upwelling winds blew 33 to 39 hours in the week.

## Caveats
- The newest reports are 6 days old (St. Joseph, South Haven, Muskegon) and 12 days old (Grand Haven). Water and fish can move a lot in a week this time of year.
- Current conditions are not live. I couldn't check today's buoy temperature, the 3-day trend, or the wind forecast. Check them before you go.
- The ratings are my estimates from only a few boat reports per port. Grand Haven has none recently.
- Conditions were rough: gusts to 44 to 47 mph in the week before. If the forecast is strong, skip the boat and use the pier or river.

## Sources
- Muskegon, St. Joseph, South Haven (2023-04-26): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3573537
- Muskegon, Grand Haven (2023-04-20): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3561fa6
- Past season, St. Joseph (2022-05-04): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
